title: Detecting pulmonary malignancy against benign nodules using noninvasive cell-free DNA fragmentomics assay
summary: A cfDNA fragmentomics AutoML ensemble distinguished malignant from benign nodules among patients with suspicious LDCT findings (AUC 0.857 in the independent validation cohort and 0.860 in a separate 99-patient test cohort). The AACR 2023 abstract reports the same result; this supports a diagnostic signal in selected, pathologically assessed patients, not mortality reduction or population-screening benefit.
ai_technology: AutoML tunes a stacked cfDNA-fragmentomics model to classify suspicious lung nodules as malignant or benign.
organization: The Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, Liaoning, China

evidence.tested: Among LDCT-suspicious patients, the ensemble distinguished pathologically classified malignant and benign nodules; validation AUC 0.857 and separate external-test AUC 0.860.
evidence.unknown: Training and validation cohorts were separated 237/118 patients and a separate 99-patient test cohort was reported; nodule status was pathologically confirmed. Sensitivity/specificity evidence does not establish improved outcomes or performance in unselected screening populations.
evidence.ai_role: AutoML tunes a stacked cfDNA-fragmentomics model to classify suspicious lung nodules as malignant or benign.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
